Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical opacity (indicated by the arrow) and an absent second rib, which are classic radiographic signs of a Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) invading local structures. In a 75-year-old long-term smoker, this malignancy is the most likely diagnosis, and the disorientation episodes may be related to paraneoplastic syndromes (e.g., SIADH) or metastatic disease associated with lung cancer.
